title: Toxicity study of heavy metals and pathogenic bacteria in PM2.5 in Nanchang City
description: Under China's atmospheric control, moderate and severe haze days almost no longer occur, but light haze days still occur. Nanchang is a typical city with mild haze occurrence, and in order to evaluate the PM2 of winter haze days and clean days in Nanchang City. 5. The toxic effects of heavy metals and pathogenic bacteria, atmospheric fine particulate matter samples were collected at the west gate of East China University of Technology in the winter of 2021 during the frequent haze season in Nanchang. The relative abundance estimation method of geoaccumulation index method was used to obtain the toxicity of heavy metals and pathogenic bacteria on clean days and haze days. The results showed that: (1) There was no difference in the content of heavy metals (As, Bi, Cd, Co, Cr, Cu, Mn, Mo, Ni, Pb, Sb, V and Zn) in the atmospheric fine particulate matter on clean and hazy days in Nanchang City, except for Zn. (2) Eight pathogenic bacteria were found in the fine particulate matter in the atmosphere on clean and hazy days in Nanchang City, among which Escherichia-Shigella, Pseudomonas and Prevotella were the main pathogenic bacteria. (3) Bacteria and bacterial pathogens in atmospheric fine particulate matter are affected by heavy metals. (4) There was no significant difference in the toxicity of heavy metals in atmospheric fine particulate matter between clean days and haze days, but the virulence of pathogenic bacteria in haze days was higher than that in clean days.
